solutions.latex:
Let $B_n$ be the amount owing after $n$ further months ($B_0=573722$).
$$B_n=573722(1.005)^n-840000\left(1.005^n-1\right)$$
Paid off when $B_n=0$:
$$0=573722(1.005)^n-840000\left(1.005^n-1\right)$$
$$(1.005)^n=\dfrac{840000}{840000-573722}$$
$$n=\ln\left(\dfrac{840000}{840000-573722}\right)\div\ln(1.005)\approx 230.4\text{ months}$$
Therefore the loan is paid off after an extra 231 months.

solutions.latex:
Let $LG=h$.

In $\triangle OGL$, $OG=3\sqrt{3}\times\cos\alpha$ and $OG=\sqrt{(3\sqrt{3})^2-h^2}$ (by Pythagoras' theorem).

In $\triangle SGL$, $SG=\sqrt{y^2-h^2}$ (by Pythagoras' theorem).

In $\triangle OSG$, by the cosine rule:
$$SG^2=OG^2+OS^2-2\times OG\times OS\times\cos 30^\circ$$
$$y^2-h^2=(3\sqrt{3})^2-h^2+10^2-2\times 3\sqrt{3}\cos\alpha\times 10\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$
$$y^2=27+100-\dfrac{90}{2}$$
$$y=\sqrt{82}\approx 9.055385\ldots\approx 9\text{ m (to the nearest metre)}$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution; 2: correct expression for SG or OG; 1: some progress towards correct answer

solutions.latex:
$S=\dfrac{D}{T}$, so $T=\dfrac{1200}{v}$ hours.

Cost of wages $=55\times 2\times\dfrac{1200}{v}=\dfrac{132000}{v}$

Cost of fuel $=\left(10+\dfrac{v^2}{100}\right)\times\dfrac{1200}{v}\times 1.50=\left(10+\dfrac{v^2}{100}\right)\times\dfrac{1800}{v}=\dfrac{18000}{v}+18v$

Total cost $=\dfrac{150000}{v}+18v$

$\dfrac{dC}{dv}=\dfrac{-150000}{v^2}+18$; stationary at $\dfrac{dC}{dv}=0$: $18v^2=150000$, $v^2=\dfrac{150000}{18}$, $v\approx 91.287\ldots\approx 91$ km/h.

$\dfrac{d^2C}{dv^2}=\dfrac{300000}{v^3}$; at $v=91$, $\dfrac{d^2C}{dv^2}=\dfrac{300000}{91^3}>0$ so a MINIMUM when $v=91$ km/h.

MINIMUM cost $=\dfrac{150000}{91}+18\times 91\approx 3286.3516\ldots\approx\$3286$ (to the nearest dollar)
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: correct solution; 3: correctly determines the first and second derivative; 2: makes some progress towards an expression for the cost; 1: some progress towards correct answer
